refuter_findings.evidence: The definition applies to an arbitrary "smooth $m$-manifold" and declares $\varphi(A\cap U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ "null in the Euclidean sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]]". That dependency begins "Fix $m\ge1$" and supplies no $\mathbb R^0$ case. Thus the definition gives no meaning to nullity on a $0$-manifold, although its stated domain includes one.

Step 2.1 infers from "$K_t\subseteq O_t$ and $K$ is compact" that an open interval $I_t$ has $K\cap(I_t\times\mathbb R^n)\subseteq I_t\times O_t$. Here [F1] uses closed cubes, so $O_t$ need not be open. For $K=\{(s,s):s\in[0,1]\}\subset[0,1]\times\mathbb R$, $t=1/2$, and the valid finite section cover $Q_{t,1}=\{1/2\}$, $O_t=\{1/2\}$; every interval about $t$ contains $s\ne t$ with $(s,s)\in K$, contradicting the claimed inclusion.

The statement quantifies over "$0\le j<r$" and then requires $K\subseteq C_j\setminus C_{j+1}$, but it defines $C_j$ only "for $j\ge1$." Thus $C_0$ is undefined in the permitted $j=0$ case. The later Euclidean Sard theorem separately sets a different $C_0:=\operatorname{Crit}(f)\cap Q_\nu$; that stipulation is absent here.

Step 3.1 states: "$E_x$ null in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. Its projection to $\mathbb R^n$ is exactly $f(K\cap W_x)$, and coordinate projection sends null sets to null sets." Coordinate projection does not preserve nullity when the source dimension is larger: $[0,1]^n\times\{0\}$ is null in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, while its projection is $[0,1]^n$, which is not null in $\mathbb R^n$. No added property of $E_x$ is cited to justify this passage.

Step 2.1 says "Because $r\ge m-n+1$ when $m>n$, one has $rn>m$, so the flat lemma ... applies." For $m=2$, $n=1$, and $r=2$, the theorem hypothesis $r>\max\{m-n,0\}=1$ holds and $r\ge m-n+1$, but $rn=2=m$, not $>m$. The cited flat-stratum lemma explicitly requires $rn>m$, so it cannot be invoked in this threshold case.

Step 2.1 proves only that $\psi(F(U))$ is null in the one target chart $V$, then step 3.1 says [L2] makes $F(U)$ null in $N$. The cited [L2] states that a set is manifold-null iff its image is null in every chart of a countable atlas. It does not license global nullity from one chart image; a transition-map/countable-localization argument is missing.

Step 1.1 says "Both $F$ and $G$ are submersions ... Hence [L1] gives $F\pitchfork G$." But [L1] is [[cor-a-submersion-is-transverse-to-every-embedded-submanifold]], whose Statement only gives $F\pitchfork Z$ for an embedded submanifold $Z\subseteq N$; it does not state transversality of two maps. The conclusion is true here by the map-transversality definition and the displayed surjective differentials, but it is not what [L1] licenses.
